beats.care: If a friend pitches a 'business' where you pay to join and earn by recruiting others, walk away. Report fraud on 1930.
beats.what: Hyderabad's Central Crime Station arrested Dig Vijay Singh, a QNET promoter, at Delhi airport as he tried to leave for Dubai.
beats.why: Police say QNET and Vihaan Direct Selling lured people with big commissions and foreign trips into a multi-level marketing scheme.

cards.body: In the Hyderabad case, 43 victims have been examined so far, with about ₹5 crore involved. Police say cases across India may add up to nearly ₹10,000 crore. A Delhi court sent him to Hyderabad on transit remand.
Warning signs: a joining fee, pressure to recruit, income promises, flashy trips and talk of 'freedom'. Real jobs pay you; they don't charge you to start.
cards.title: how do i spot an mlm trap?

cards.body: Police say the network was allegedly run from Dubai, and they are now checking foreign nationals' roles and cross-border money trails.

opts: You earn mainly by recruiting others
cards.q: What's the biggest red flag in a scheme like this?
cards.why: When income depends on bringing in new members, the money runs out once recruiting slows.

hook: Big returns, foreign trips, *recruit friends*: how this alleged scam worked

learn.t: Schemes where you earn mainly by recruiting others are banned in India under the 1978 money circulation schemes law.
